llm.summary: This is a disclosed Chinese K12 classroom-coaching skill that reads teaching context and student grouping signals to help teachers run interactive lessons, with no executable code or hidden behavior found.

dimensions.detail: Use of persistent memory and timing capability is proportionate to classroom records and activity timing, and the skill defines degradation paths when those platform capabilities are unavailable.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package consists of Markdown guidance and a JSON schema only; no executable scripts, remote payload retrieval, dependencies, or install-time commands were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Trigger examples are somewhat broad and it can generate a fallback question chain when no upstream draft exists, but both behaviors are within the classroom-interaction purpose and adjacent-skill routing is documented.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It writes classroom interaction logs, but only as teacher-confirmed entries, avoids student names in those logs, and includes view/correct/delete/pause/share/export controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's purpose is classroom interaction coaching for teachers; reading lesson plans, class profile, student tiers, and weakness rankings is disclosed and directly supports grouping, question pacing, and cold-call avoidance.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this for Chinese-language K12 teacher workflows where teachers are comfortable sharing lesson-plan context and pseudonymous student tier/weakness signals with the skill. Before using it in another region or language, localize the curriculum assumptions and crisis-support channels, and keep teacher confirmation enabled for any classroom-record writeback.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger examples relate to classroom interaction requests; adjacent requests are routed to planner, exam, analyzer, or assignment skills, so this is a precision issue rather than unsafe behavior.
[SDI-1] expected: The fallback question-chain generation and read access to lesson plans/student-tier data are explicitly disclosed and used for in-class implementation; write scope remains limited to interactionLogs.
[SQP-3] expected: The artifacts are Chinese-only, but shared platform guidance states the package is designed for Chinese Mainland K12 use and requires localization before other regions, so this is deployment guidance rather than hidden locale forcing.
